body:
The current manuscript predicts the native RTX intervention outcomes, but global serialization can lose generation speed and ordinary batched speculation can change the fixed reference output. This additive experiment uses the original intervention to diagnose the incoming-state/current-call interaction, then tests a local attention constraint that retains projection/FFN batching.

The primary cost gate gives target-only the same UB4/query-batch prefill as the speculative candidate and bypasses observer metadata/synchronization when capture is disabled. On the original 19 exposed tasks, four repetitions produce 76/76 reference-matching complete ID/EOG-cap128 arrays for each mode. The candidate achieves 1.256× generation and 1.077× whole-request geometric-mean speedups from per-task median ratios; generation is faster on 19/19 tasks and whole requests on 16/19.

Evidence and controls:
- 12 engineering trajectories qualify capture/sham. 24 complete native donors reproduce the original arrays; 48 paid real-state forks expose a current-call effect on /15 and a donor-state/current-path interaction on /25. All 24 same-path fork decisions match naturally reached native decisions; source state remains unchanged. Pinned logical KV parsing checks every serialized byte.
- The retained k2 panel has 171 requests: full serialization and per-query attention preserve outputs but generation remains slower. The initial balanced k3 panel has 304 requests: ordinary k3 fails /25 and /18 in every repetition (68/76 matches), while both constraints pass 76/76. Its 1.852× request ratio includes prefill savings and observer-wrapper costs, so it is kept separate from the primary matched-prefill result.
- The primary panel has 152 requests after 8 complete CLI qualification trajectories. Across the study, 60 complete CLI trajectories, 627 measured requests and 33 excluded warmups total 720 completed generation requests; 48 forks and 1,278 auxiliary forwards are accounted separately. All recorded hash/source/output checks pass, and model/runtime assets are unchanged. A zero-model preparation failure and a legacy command-metadata correction are explicitly retained.

Scope: both target and draft attention are constrained in prefill and continuation; this is not a target-only causal ablation, minimal-constraint proof or general invariance theorem. All tasks are exposed, and no functional accuracy, held-out/cross-stack transfer, energy/throughput or production-release claim is made. Existing [LLM-42](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.17768v2) and [batch-invariant inference](https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/defeating-nondeterminism-in-llm-inference/) remain related-work baselines. The next gate is target/draft and prefill/continuation ablation followed by exposure-audited transfer.

Review `benchmarks/rtx_consistency_contract_v1/README.md`, `REPORT_ZH.md`, `SCOPE.md`, `REPRODUCE.md`, and the results/provenance directories. Source versions are local experiment commits indexed by file hashes; a complete local Git bundle and content-addressed raw-evidence archive accompany the workspace deliverables. Weights, released DLLs and raw telemetry are excluded from GitHub.

Validation: all 67 uploaded blobs were read back and matched their local Git blob hashes; comparison to main e87291d confirms one commit containing only additions under this new benchmark directory. Manuscript files, prior results and the #56 selector NO-GO are unchanged. This extends #57 and #58 without requiring their merge.
title: Extend RTX diagnosis with native state crossing and local attention efficiency gates
